description: FIND-018 (iter-1) flagged that the gh-issue-escalation pattern `r"['\"]escalation['\"]"` only matched quoted occurrences and was inconsistent with sibling patterns using `\b...\b`. The iter-2 fix at lib/group_j.py:63 narrows it to `r"--label\s*[=]?\s*['\"]?escalation['\"]?"` — a context-bound match requiring the literal `--label` immediately preceding `escalation`. This catches `--label escalation`, `--label=escalation`, `--label "escalation"`, but DOES NOT catch the most common subprocess-list form in Python: `subprocess.run(["gh", "issue", "create", "--label", "escalation"])`. Between the `--label` token and the `escalation` token, the source contains `",\s*"` (closing quote, comma, space, opening quote), which `\s*[=]?\s*['\"]?` does not match. The sibling patterns for `needs-login`, `needs-human`, `please-review` all use `\b<token>\b` (no `--label` context binding), so they catch the list-literal form. The fix correctly addresses the comment/docstring false-positive concern (the spec body contains the word `escalation` in many sentences) but reintroduces a real bypass. A defensible regex is `(?:--label[\s=,"' ]+)?(?:^|["',\s\[])escalation(?:$|["',\s\]])` or a two-rule split: (a) `--label\s*[=]?\s*['\"]?escalation['\"]?` for command-line forms AND (b) `["']escalation["']` for list-literal forms, with the docstring/comment false-positive handled by excluding lines that start with `#` or are inside a multi-line string. The current single regex closes one bypass and opens another.
